firing.source:
declare const foo: any;
export const r = foo?.[0]!;

findings.message: An optional chain returns `undefined` by design when a link is nullish, so asserting the result non-null contradicts the reason the `?.` was written. The assertion is erased at compile time and the `undefined` still arrives at runtime, which turns a guard the author asked for into a crash the types promised could not happen. Handle the `undefined` case instead, or drop the `?.` if the value cannot actually be nullish.
